criteria.statement: Services update, deployments preview/deploy/route-attach, and DNS commands use a pre-publish EOSE activation barrier, a bounded per-attempt result timeout, and configurable idempotent result retries.
A signed plain ContextVM request and response complete through the client and server transports together on local and public relay identities.

When relay A fails to establish a reply subscription and the terminal result is available only through subscribed relay B, the client still receives the result and accounts only for established subscriptions.

If a completed deployment preview response is lost, the client timeout republishes the same idempotent logical request and Bahia replays the cached desired_state_hash response without invoking the handler twice.
Encrypted mode uses real local-key NIP-44/NIP-59 request and response crypto with outer-wrapper and signed-inner correlation validation.
Terminal responses are retried on server publication failure, duplicate idempotent requests replay responses persisted for 24 hours, and multi-relay partial publication success does not retry.

Failures expose request method, event id, d-tag, configured/subscribed/failed relays, publish count, attempt count, and per-relay publish outcomes for correlation with server handler and publication logs.

When the relay sidecar is enabled, ContextVM request subscriptions, progress acknowledgments, and terminal responses use the deduplicated union of the sidecar and configured ContextVM relays, falling back to browser relays when the ContextVM list is empty.
